specs.title: Leap Incentives — Lookups
specs.description:
Check which rebate programs a customer qualifies for, and keep that answer current as their situation changes. Three operations share one request shape:

  * `POST /beta/incentives/lookups` is the first call for a customer. It stores the customer and their devices, resolves the serving utility from the address, and evaluates eligibility.
  * `POST /beta/incentives/refreshes` re-evaluates a customer you have already looked up, against their stored address and devices. Send it to pick up newly launched programs and updated amounts, or to add, update, or remove individual devices.
  * `POST /beta/incentives/overrides` rebuilds an existing customer from a fresh request body: it re-resolves the address and serving utility, replaces the device set, and clears the customer attributes you previously supplied. Use it to correct a customer record before any application is submitted.

Authenticate every call with your Leap API key as a bearer token. Your account is identified by that key, so the customers, devices, and applications you read and write are always your own.

include.title: Look up incentives
include.description: Check which rebate programs a customer qualifies for. Send the customer's address, classification, and devices; Leap returns the total incentive amount, a per-program breakdown, and a Connect URL the customer can use to apply.

include.title: Refresh incentives
include.description: Re-run eligibility for a customer you've already looked up, using their stored address and devices — no need to resend them. Use this to pick up newly launched programs or updated incentive amounts.

include.title: Override incentives
include.description: Replace an existing customer's device list, then re-run eligibility. Use this when a customer's equipment has changed. The previous device set is discarded.

schemaDescriptions.EligibilityRequest.create_application: Create the Connect application records for this lookup's eligible programs, so the returned `connect_url` is a link the customer can open. Provisioning runs in the background and is normally in place within seconds. Defaults to `false`: lookup-only integrations are unaffected and no applications are created for them. No effect on billing or rate limits.
schemaDescriptions.EligibilityRequest.include_preview: Include your own unpublished partner offer in the results so you can test it before publishing. Only your own offer is ever included. Utility, state, and market programs are unaffected. Defaults to `false`.
schemaDescriptions.EligibilityResult.connect_url: Deep link to hand the customer so they can apply: `https://connect.incentives.leap.energy/{company}/refId/{reference_id}`, where `{company}` is your registration nickname. **Omitted entirely when the lookup surfaces no eligible incentive** — there is nothing to apply for, so check that the field is present before showing a link.
schemaDescriptions.IncentiveSummary.ongoing_amount: Total recurring incentives across all eligible programs, **per year**.
schemaDescriptions.IncentiveSummary.upfront_amount: Reserved for a payment kind Leap does not pay yet, so it is always 0. Read `install_amount` for the one-time total.
schemaDescriptions.IncentiveSummary.install_amount: Total one-time incentives across all eligible programs, paid at install time.
schemaDescriptions.EligibleProgram.upfront_amount: Reserved for a payment kind Leap does not pay yet, so it is always 0. Read `install_amount` for this program's one-time incentive.
schemaDescriptions.EligibleProgram.install_amount: This program's one-time incentive, paid at install time.
schemaDescriptions.RefreshIncentivesRequest.create_applicat: Create the Connect application records for this refresh's eligible programs, so the returned `connect_url` is a link the customer can open. It matches the flag on **Look up incentives** and defaults to `false`. Only a refresh that changes something has anything to create: one that supplies `customer_devices`, `customer_details` or a removal. A bare re-evaluation creates nothing, flag or no flag. No effect on billing or rate limits.
schemaDescriptions.RefreshIncentivesRequest.eiaid: Optional utility override, matching the one on **Look up incentives**. Supply an EIA utility id to re-resolve the customer's serving utility instead of reusing the one on file. Leap re-selects candidate programs against it, re-runs eligibility, and keeps the override for later calls on this customer.
schemaDescriptions.EligibleProgram.name: Program name as shown to the customer. Leap sets this for utility, state, and market programs; for your own partner offer it is the offer name you configure in the portal.
schemaDescriptions.EligibleProgram.program_identifier: Stable identifier for this program — your offer's identifier for a partner offer, or the catalog identifier (for example `PGE-ART`) otherwise. Use it to correlate the same program across lookups.
schemaDescriptions.EligibleProgram.is_partner_offer: `true` when this entry is your own partner offer (which bundles one or more underlying programs); `false` for utility, state, and market rebate programs. Use it to separate your offer from rebates in your own UI.
schemaDescriptions.MatchedTier.incentive_amount: Tier total across the devices that passed this tier's requirements; per-device outcomes are in `device_results[]`. Units follow `payment_type`: `UPFRONT` and `INSTALL` amounts are one-time, `ONGOING` amounts are per year.
schemaDescriptions.PartnerBranding: Your brand name and logo as configured on your Leap account, so a surface rendering these results can show your branding without a second call.
schemaDescriptions.CustomerDeviceRef: One installation. New installations name their catalog device with `device_id`. On **Refresh incentives**, `customer_device_id` instead targets an installation already on file, for an in-place update.
schemaDescriptions.CustomerDeviceRef.device_id: The catalog device's `id`, from **Search device catalog** or the portal's Device profile mapping. Required on a new installation. Optional when `customer_device_id` targets an installation already on file, and must match that installation's catalog device when you do send it. A `device_id` that is not in the catalog is rejected with 422 `INVALID_DEVICE_ID`.
schemaDescriptions.EligibilityRequest.customer_devices:
One entry per installation, at least one and at most 50. Each names a catalog `device_id` and an optional `partner_device_reference` that tells two installations of the same device apart. The inline `details` object carries per-installation attributes, for example `customer_device.purchase_price` or `customer_device.installation_date`.

On **Override incentives** this list replaces the customer's device set: every installation on file is discarded first, so their `customer_device_id`s are regenerated.
schemaDescriptions.CustomerDeviceRef.customer_device_id: Identifies one installation — this customer, this catalog device, your device reference. Leap assigns it on the first lookup and echoes it back in `customer_devices[]`; it is stable across later lookups and refreshes, and is regenerated only by **Override incentives**, which replaces the device set. Send it on **Refresh incentives** to update that installation in place; it is rejected with 400 on lookups and overrides.
schemaDescriptions.RefreshIncentivesRequest.customer_device: Optional device merge set. An entry carrying a `customer_device_id` updates that installation in place; an entry without one adds a new installation. Installations already on file that you don't list are left untouched — sending a subset never deletes the rest.
schemaDescriptions.RefreshIncentivesRequest.remove_customer: Remove installations by `customer_device_id`. Ids that don't match a device on this customer are ignored, so retries are safe.
schemaDescriptions.RefreshIncentivesRequest.remove_device_r: Remove installations by `partner_device_reference`. Every installation with a matching reference is removed; unknown references are ignored.
schemaDescriptions.PartnerBranding.logo_url: URL to your logo, as configured on your Leap account. Null when no logo is configured.
schemaDescriptions.EligibilityCheck.source_program_identifi: On a partner offer, the program this check came from — your offer's identifier for checks on the offer itself, or the identifier of an underlying program for checks it inherits. Null on rebate programs.
schemaDescriptions.EligibilityRequest.customer_details:
Customer attributes you're supplying, keyed by field name, for example `{"customer.utility_account_number": "0123456789"}`. Values are always strings. Facts about one installation go in that entry's `details` object instead.

Send project costs here, once per customer. `customer.installation_cost` is the services total for the whole job, before tax: labor, materials, and permits. `customer.total_project_cost` is the deal total including tax. Each device's equipment price goes in that device's `details` as `customer_device.purchase_price`.

In cost-based amounts, `customer.installation_cost` replaces each device's installation cost and the regional estimate. In installation cost checks, it stands in for the device's `customer_device.installation_cost`. Each cost calculation counts it once, and each program and each tier is its own calculation. Leap doesn't split it between devices or programs. It stays on file until you clear it. Send it as an empty string on a refresh, or leave it out of an override body.

Leap ignores a value that is negative, above 1,000,000,000, or written with more than six decimal places. Device-level costs apply instead. Text that isn't a number returns 400. A zero is a real zero. No calculation reads `customer.total_project_cost` yet.

An unrecognised key returns 400 and no incentives. The [Requirements reference](/setup-data-preferences) lists every key and its value form.

Omit or leave empty if you have none. Maximum 100 entries.
schemaDescriptions.RefreshIncentivesRequest.customer_detail:
Customer attributes to merge before re-evaluating, keyed by field name. Values are always strings. A key you send replaces what's on file, and a key you leave out is untouched. Use this to fill in facts as you learn them, rather than repeating a lookup.

Send project costs here, once per customer. `customer.installation_cost` is the services total for the whole job, before tax: labor, materials, and permits. `customer.total_project_cost` is the deal total including tax. Each device's equipment price goes in that device's `details` as `customer_device.purchase_price`.

In cost-based amounts, `customer.installation_cost` replaces each device's installation cost and the regional estimate. In installation cost checks, it stands in for the device's `customer_device.installation_cost`. Each cost calculation counts it once, and each program and each tier is its own calculation. Leap doesn't split it between devices or programs. It stays on file until you clear it. Send it as an empty string on a refresh, or leave it out of an override body.

Leap ignores a value that is negative, above 1,000,000,000, or written with more than six decimal places. Device-level costs apply instead. Text that isn't a number returns 400. A zero is a real zero. No calculation reads `customer.total_project_cost` yet.

An unrecognised key returns 400 and no incentives. The [Requirements reference](/setup-data-preferences) lists every key and its value form.

Omit or leave empty for no attribute changes. Maximum 100 entries.
schemaDescriptions.CustomerDeviceRef.details:
Attributes for this one installation, keyed by field name, for example `{"customer_device.purchase_price": "699.00"}`. Values are always strings. Facts about the customer go in the request's `customer_details` object instead.

Send the equipment price here as `customer_device.purchase_price`. If you hold one services total for the whole job, send it once as `customer.installation_cost` in `customer_details`. Don't repeat it here, because a repeated total counts once per device. In cost-based amounts, the customer-level value replaces this device's installation cost and the regional estimate. Each cost calculation counts it once, not once per device. In installation cost checks, it stands in for this device's `customer_device.installation_cost`.

An unrecognised key returns 400 and no incentives. The [Requirements reference](/setup-data-preferences) lists every key and its value form.

Maximum 50 entries.
schemaDescriptions.EligibleProgram.included_leap_program_id: Partner offers only: identifiers of the underlying programs this offer covers for this customer. Empty for every other kind of entry.
schemaDescriptions.CustomerClassification: The customer or site classification used to determine eligibility. `RESIDENTIAL` and `COMMERCIAL` are the long-standing values; `MULTIFAMILY` and `MANUFACTURED_HOME` exist because rebate qualification differs across single-family, multifamily, and manufactured housing.
schemaDescriptions.CustomerDeviceRefEcho.customer_device_id: Leap's identifier for this installation. Store it — it's how you address that specific device on later calls.
schemaDescriptions.EligibilityRequest.reference_id: Your stable identifier for this customer. Leap uses it to recognise a returning customer, and you'll send it again on **Refresh incentives**, **Override incentives**, and when searching applications. It's scoped to you — another partner using the same value is a different customer.
schemaDescriptions.EligibleProgram.operator_name: The utility or agency that operates the program, as shown to the customer. On your own partner offer it is the operator name you configure in the portal. Null when Leap holds no display name for the program.
schemaDescriptions.EligibleProgram.covered_programs: Partner offers only: the rebate programs bundled into this offer that the customer qualified for, and whose value is summed into this entry's amounts. Empty for every other kind of entry.
schemaDescriptions.EligibleProgram.description: Partner offers only: the offer description shown to the customer, as configured in the portal. Null for rebate programs.
schemaDescriptions.EligibleProgram.display_name: Partner offers only: the branded offer name shown to the customer, as configured in the portal. Null for rebate programs.
schemaDescriptions.EligibleProgram.logo_url: Partner offers only: URL to the logo shown alongside the offer, as configured in the portal. Null for rebate programs.
schemaDescriptions.EligibleProgram.terms_url: Partner offers only: URL to the offer's terms and conditions, as configured in the portal. Null for rebate programs.
schemaDescriptions.CoveredProgram.identifier: Identifier of the bundled program. Use it to tell the covered programs apart across lookups; it is not a value any other endpoint accepts.
schemaDescriptions.EligibilityRequest.eiaid: Optional utility override. Supply it when you already know the customer's serving utility and the address-based match is unavailable or ambiguous: Leap uses this EIA utility id to select candidate programs instead of resolving the utility from the address. On this path the address isn't geocoded, so the response omits the `geocoding` block and any stored coordinates are left as they are. A value matching no utility fails the same way an unserved address does (404 `NO_UTILITY_AT_ADDRESS`).

replacements.from: The category UUID is deliberately not accepted here — `device_category.id` is minted per environment, so a UUID that works against staging does not address the same category in production.
replacements.to: Address a category by name: the category's own id is specific to one Leap environment and is not accepted here.

replacements.from: An id that matches no active, non-test device is simply absent from the results rather than an error, so a caller must match responses back to the ids it asked for.
replacements.to: An id that matches no device currently in the catalog is simply absent from the results rather than an error, so match the responses back to the ids you asked for.

include.title: Search device catalog
include.description: Find the catalog `device_id` for a product, or browse the catalog when you have no search term. Use it to map your product catalog to Leap's programmatically instead of by hand. A query parameter this endpoint does not recognise returns 400 rather than being ignored, so a misspelled filter fails loudly.

include.title: List saved devices
include.description: List the devices you've saved, most recently saved first. Each entry carries the full catalog record plus your own optional label. Saving the products you sell keeps them on hand without a catalog search every time. Results are scoped to your account; page through them with `limit` and `offset`.

include.title: Save a device
include.description: Add a catalog device to your saved list, or relabel one you already saved. Repeating the call updates the existing entry instead of adding a second one. A catalog device Leap has retired returns 404.

include.title: Remove a saved device
include.description: Remove a device from your saved list. The catalog device is untouched, and so is any lookup that referenced it. Removing a device you have not saved also returns 204, so retries are safe.

schemaDescriptions.PartnerDeviceResponse: One device in Leap's catalog. Send its `id` as the `device_id` on a lookup. Specification fields such as `capacity_kw` or `seer2_rating` are populated where Leap holds data for that device type, and are null otherwise.
schemaDescriptions.PartnerDeviceResponse.device_category: The device's category name, and the stable way to address a category: `hvac`, `ev_charger`, `solar_storage`, `water_heater`, `smart_thermostat`, `weatherization`, `vehicle`, `meter`, `panel_make_ready`, `solar_panel`. It is the same value the `category` query parameter takes, so you can bucket a page of results without a second call.
schemaDescriptions.PartnerDeviceResponse.device_category_id: Leap's identifier for the device's category. It is specific to one Leap environment, so key on `device_category` instead when you store or compare categories.
schemaDescriptions.SavedDeviceUpsertRequest.label: Your own name for the device, to help you find it later. Omit the key to keep the current label, send null or a blank string to clear it, send text to set it. Maximum 256 characters.
schemaDescriptions.SavedDeviceResponse.device_id: Catalog device UUID. This is the `device_id` you send on a lookup.
schemaDescriptions.SavedDeviceResponse.label: Your own name for the device, when you set one. Null otherwise.
schemaDescriptions.SavedDeviceResponse.created_at: When you first saved this device.
schemaDescriptions.SavedDevicePage.total: Total devices on your saved list, ignoring paging.

replacements.from: The underlying column is open jsonb that internal tooling writes to freely, so responses carry an allowlist rather than the whole map.
replacements.to: Responses carry an allowlist of keys rather than everything Leap stores against a program.

replacements.from:
Filter DSL. Comma-separated field=value pairs. Supported fields: program_type, transmission_region, enabled, device_category, customer_classification, state. An unrecognised field is rejected with 400 rather than ignored.

device_category and customer_classification read a null on a LEAP_DEFINITIONS row as a WILDCARD matching every value, which is how candidate selection already reads them. Repeating either field ORs the values, so device_category=ev_charger,device_category=solar_storage means either — the reading a multi-select control needs. Every other field keeps its last value if repeated.

state matches a program the same two ways the by_state facet places one: its own metadata.state_province when it has one, otherwise every state its eiaids reach. All comparisons are case-insensitive.

Example: transmission_region=CAISO,enabled=true,device_category=ev_charger
replacements.to:
Comma-separated `field=value` pairs, combined with AND. Supported fields: `program_type`, `transmission_region`, `enabled`, `device_category`, `customer_classification` and `state`. For example, `filter=program_type=VPP,enabled=true` returns the enabled programs that put a device under control.

An unrecognised field returns 400. `enabled` must be `true` or `false`; anything else returns 400. A pair with no `=` is ignored, so `filter=VPP` returns the unfiltered catalog. A `filter` over 500 characters returns 400.

With no `enabled` filter the response mixes enabled and disabled programs, and each row carries its own `enabled` flag.

Repeat `device_category` or `customer_classification` to match any of several values: `device_category=ev_charger,device_category=solar_storage` matches either. A `LEAP_DEFINITIONS` program that names no device category or classification matches every value. Every other field keeps its last value if repeated.

`state` matches a program's own state when it has one. Otherwise it matches the state Leap records for each utility the program serves.

Comparisons for `device_category`, `customer_classification`, `state` and `enabled` ignore case. Send `program_type` and `transmission_region` in upper case, such as `VPP` and `CAISO`.

replacements.from: Free text over label, program_identifier and metadata.operator_name. Whitespace splits it into tokens and every token must match, so more words narrow the result. Composes with filter.
replacements.to:
Free-text search over each program's `label`, `program_identifier` and `metadata.operator_name`. Matching is case-insensitive and finds the text anywhere in those fields. Every word must match, so adding words narrows the result. Combines with `filter` and `exclude_source`.

A value over 200 characters returns 400. Leap reads the first 10 words, and the first 64 characters of each.

replacements.from:
When true, the response carries a facets object holding the total row count for the current filter plus per-value counts for device category, customer classification and state. Each dimension is counted with its own narrowing removed, so a dropdown can show what switching to another value would return.

Cannot be combined with page_token, and a request sending both is rejected with 400. Facets describe the filter rather than the page, so they do not change as you walk it, while counting them costs several aggregate passes over the table. Request them once on the first call and carry them across the remaining pages.
replacements.to:
Set to `true` to add a `facets` object to the response. It counts the programs matching your `filter`, `q` and `exclude_source` across every page. It also breaks them down by device category, customer classification, state and program type.

Send it on the first page only: a request with both `include_facets=true` and a `page_token` returns 400. The counts describe the whole filtered listing, so they are the same on every page. Defaults to `false`.

replacements.from:
Comma-separated program sources to leave out: LEAP_DEFINITIONS, INCENTIVES_DB, PARTNER_OFFER. An unrecognised value is rejected with 400 rather than ignored.

Applies to the rows and to the facet counts alike, so a total never describes a population the data does not. Absent means no source is excluded, which is what every existing caller gets.
replacements.to:
Comma-separated program sources to leave out: `LEAP_DEFINITIONS`, `INCENTIVES_DB` or `PARTNER_OFFER`. For example, `exclude_source=PARTNER_OFFER` lists catalog programs without any partner offers. An unrecognised value returns 400, and so does a value over 200 characters.

The exclusion applies to the listed programs and to the `facets` counts alike. Omit it to include every source.

Cursor from a previous response's `next_page_token`. Follow it until it is absent to walk the whole catalog. Replay a token only with the `filter` that produced it. Programs are ordered by `program_identifier`, so a program added below your cursor part-way through a walk is missed rather than duplicated. This route pages with `page_size` and `page_token` only: `limit` and `offset` return 400.
Rows per page. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 200; a larger value is clamped rather than rejected.
The program's `program_identifier`. This route spells the path segment `programIdentifier` while every other program route uses `program_id`; both take the same value.

include.title: List programs
include.description: Browse Leap's program catalog. The catalog is shared across partners. A program you read here is not necessarily one your account can claim. Narrow it with `filter`, and page through it with `page_size` and `page_token`.

include.title: Get a program
include.description: Retrieve one program by its `program_identifier`, the same value **Look up incentives** returns on each eligible program. An identifier Leap does not hold returns 404.

include.title: List approved devices
include.description: List the Approved Product List (APL) entries for a program: the catalog devices it pays a rebate on. Each entry names the catalog `device_id`, the tier it is bound to when it is tier-specific, and the APL publication it came from. Resolve a `device_id` with **Search device catalog**.

schemaDescriptions.ProgramSummaryResponse: One program in Leap's program catalog. The catalog is shared across partners and covers utility, state and market programs. A program you read here is not necessarily one your account can claim.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramSummaryResponse.program_identifie: Stable identifier for the program, and the value **Look up incentives** returns as `program_identifier` on each eligible program. Send it as the `program_id` path segment on the other program routes.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramSummaryResponse.eiaids: Every EIA utility id this program serves. A customer qualifies on the utility dimension when the utility resolved from their address appears in this list. An empty list means the program has no utility footprint and is never selected on that dimension.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramSummaryResponse.enabled: Whether Leap currently evaluates this program. A disabled program never appears in a lookup result. Filter on it with `filter=enabled=true` or `filter=enabled=false`.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramSummaryResponse.program_type: Whether the program puts the customer's device under control. Leap sets `VPP` on programs that control or dispatch the device. Examples include demand response, managed charging and virtual power plant programs. `REBATE` marks programs that pay toward buying or installing the device without controlling it afterwards. Read `operator_type` for who the customer enrolls through.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramOperatorType: Who the customer enrolls through. `LEAP` marks Leap's own programs, even when a utility or grid operator runs the underlying program. `metadata.operator_name` names that operator. `PARTNER` marks every partner offer. For every other catalog program, `UTILITY`, `STATE`, `LOCAL`, `FEDERAL` or `PROVINCIAL` gives the kind of public operator. The field is omitted when Leap hasn't recorded the operator, or recorded a value outside these kinds. Treat an absent field and a null one the same way, as unknown rather than none. `metadata.operator_type` is the raw catalog value, which can fall outside this list. Read this top-level field instead.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramSummaryResponse.device_categories: Every device category the program covers. Leap offers the program to a customer with a device in any listed category, or in `device_category`. Empty when the program names only `device_category`. The list `filter` and the category facets read `device_category` only.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramFacets:
Counts that describe the whole filtered listing, not only the page in `data`. Present only when the request sets `include_facets=true`.

Each per-value map is counted without its own filter field. A dropdown can then show what choosing another value would return. For example, `by_state` ignores your `state` filter and applies every other one. The maps therefore don't add up to `total`.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramFacets.enabled_count: How many of the `total` programs are enabled. Leap evaluates only enabled programs in a lookup.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramFacets.by_device_category: Programs per device category, keyed by lower-case category and counted without your `device_category` filter. A `LEAP_DEFINITIONS` program that names no device category matches every category under a filter. It appears in no bucket here, and `wildcard_category_count` counts those programs.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramFacets.by_customer_classification: Programs per customer classification, keyed by upper-case value and counted without your `customer_classification` filter. A `LEAP_DEFINITIONS` program that names no classification matches every classification under a filter. It appears in no bucket here, and `wildcard_classification_count` counts those programs.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramFacets.by_state:
Programs per state, keyed by upper-case state code and counted without your `state` filter.

A program with its own state counts in that state. A program without one counts once in the state Leap records for each utility it serves. Leap records one state per utility, so a utility serving several states places its programs in one of them. A program with neither appears in no bucket.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramFacets.by_program_type: Programs per `program_type`, such as `VPP` and `REBATE`, counted without your `program_type` filter. Each program counts once, so this map splits distinct programs by type. The state maps can't give that split, because they count a program once per state.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramFacets.by_state_program_type: `by_state` split by `program_type`: keyed by state code, then by program type, to a count. For each state, the counts sum to that state's `by_state` value.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramFacets.placed_program_count:
Distinct programs that appear in at least one `by_state` bucket. The sum of `by_state` counts a program once per state, so it is larger whenever a program spans states.

`total` minus this value is the number of matching programs Leap can't place in any state. It is counted under your whole filter, including `state`, so it covers the same programs as `total`.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramFacets.wildcard_category_count: `LEAP_DEFINITIONS` programs that name no device category, so they match every category when you filter on one. They appear in no `by_device_category` bucket. Add this number to each bucket for per-category counts that agree with filtering. Counted without your `device_category` filter.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramFacets.wildcard_classification_co: The same count for customer classification: `LEAP_DEFINITIONS` programs that name no classification, so they serve every customer segment. Add this number to each `by_customer_classification` bucket for counts that agree with filtering. Counted without your `customer_classification` filter.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramListResponse: One page of catalog programs, plus the cursor for the next page.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramListResponse.next_page_token: Cursor for the next page, absent on the last page. Pass it back as `page_token`, with the same filter that produced it.
schemaDescriptions.RequirementSource: Where the definition came from. `LEAP_DEFINITIONS` marks programs Leap defines itself. Leap sets these to `VPP`. `INCENTIVES_DB` marks programs imported from the public program catalog, and each is `VPP` or `REBATE`. `PARTNER_OFFER` marks a partner offer, which a partner account configures rather than Leap.
schemaDescriptions.CustomerClassification: The customer or site class this program serves. `RESIDENTIAL` and `COMMERCIAL` are the long-standing values; `MULTIFAMILY` and `MANUFACTURED_HOME` exist because rebate qualification differs across single-family, multifamily and manufactured housing.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramApprovedDeviceResponse: One Approved Product List entry: a catalog device this program pays a rebate on.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramApprovedDeviceResponse.device_id: Catalog device UUID. It is the same identifier **Search device catalog** returns as `id`, and the same one you send as `device_id` on a lookup.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramApprovedDeviceResponse.tier_id: The incentive tier this device is bound to. Absent when the entry is not tier-specific.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramApprovedDeviceResponse.apl_source: The Approved Product List publication this entry came from.
schemaDescriptions.ProgramApprovedDeviceResponse.apl_versio: The version of that Approved Product List publication.

include.title: Search applications
include.description: Search and filter the applications you're tracking. Returns a paginated list, filterable by reference ID or status.

include.title: Get application
include.description: Retrieve a single application in full, including customer information and device details.

include.title: Update application
include.description:
Provide the information you're supplying on behalf of the customer — customer details, device data, purchase and installation dates, contractor info. Only include the fields you want to change; omitted fields keep their current values.

Status and system identifiers (`id`, `customer_id`, `program_id`) are read-only and can't be changed here.

include.title: List attachments
include.description: List the attachments on one or more applications. Pass `application_id` (with an `attachment_type`) for a single application, or `application_ids` (comma-separated) for several.

include.title: Upload attachment
include.description: Create a signed URL for uploading an attachment. Upload the file to that URL with a PUT request, then confirm it with the commit endpoint.

include.title: Commit attachment upload
include.description: Confirm an attachment after the file has been uploaded to its signed URL. This finalizes the attachment on the application.

include.title: Download attachment
include.description: Get a signed URL for downloading an attachment. The URL is valid for one hour.

include.title: Delete attachment
include.description: Permanently delete an attachment. This removes the file and its record and can't be undone.

schemaDescriptions.CustomerDevice.quantity: **Deprecated.** Each device record stands for one physical unit, and no incentive calculation reads this field. Send each unit of a model as its own `customer_devices[]` entry on the lookup, with its own `partner_device_reference`.
schemaDescriptions.CustomerDevicePatchRequest.quantity: **Deprecated.** Leave it at 1 or omit it. No incentive calculation reads it, so a value above 1 doesn't raise the amount. Send each unit of a model as its own `customer_devices[]` entry on the lookup, with its own `partner_device_reference`.
